title: Understanding Intrinsic Socioeconomic Biases in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured intrinsic socioeconomic biases against religious groups. Specifically, it quantified the tendency of LLMs to associate terms representing different religions with terms representing poverty versus wealth using a fill-in-the-mask task, which was evaluated using a Poverty Association Ratio (PAR).
findings: Falcon and Llama 2 exhibited significant socioeconomic biases, strongly associating 'Muslim' with poverty and 'Jewish' with wealth. GPT-2 also showed bias, with 'Hindu' having the highest association with poverty. BERT demonstrated the least socioeconomic bias related to religion, with associations for all tested religious groups remaining close to the neutral baseline.
